note: Discovery leads for accounting topic workers (phase 2). LITERACY level with real mechanics: teach what each accounting concept IS and why it matters, with simple original examples and arithmetic. The phase-2 introduction-to-business accounting-basics lesson already covers the overview — these topics go one level deeper (the actual equation mechanics, statement shapes, and cycle steps), still without journalizing exercises beyond illustrations.

tierA.useFor: THE backbone for financial accounting topics (equation, statements, cycle, debits/credits, AR/AP, inventory, depreciation, accrual). managerial accounting, cost behavior, fixed/variable costs, break-even, budgeting

accounting terms (often JS-walled — verify via Wayback or use CFI instead)

cautions: MECHANICS AT LITERACY LEVEL: teach the equation, the statement shapes, and the cycle steps with simple original arithmetic examples (e.g. assets = liabilities + equity with small numbers; break-even in units with a lemonade-stand example). Illustrative journal entries OK (≤6 lines) but no full journalizing exercises.
GAAP vs IFRS: teach as 'two major sets of standards, most U.S. companies follow GAAP' — factually, no advocacy; do not teach jurisdiction-specific tax rules.

STATEMENT SHAPES: income statement = revenues − expenses; balance sheet = the equation in statement form; cash flow = operating/investing/financing sections. Teach the shapes and what each is FOR, not the mechanics of preparing them.
SIBLING SUBJECTS: finance (own subject) owns time-value/valuation depth; introduction-to-business accounting-basics owns the overview — reference only.
break-even-analysis: formula is break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost per unit) — THE one formula this subject teaches; everything else at concept level.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D (≥1 C, ≥1 D per topic; max 3 of 5 per slot). Verify keys from the file yourself. BANNED: 'Which statement best defines X used in this lesson?' stems — write topic-specific questions (e.g. 'What does the accounting equation show?', 'Which event increases assets?').
